title: Model Engineering & Routing
tierLabel: Code you write, builds on context signals from Tier 2
summary: The programmatic version of /model: deciding, per task or per step, which model tier handles a request — instead of one model handling everything at the same price.
whyItMatters: Model price differences between tiers are often 5-10x. Routing simple, high-confidence steps to a cheap model and reserving expensive models for genuinely hard steps can cut aggregate cost sharply without materially hurting quality.

concepts.heading: Static routing by task type
concepts.body: The simplest form: classify the incoming task (by keyword, regex, or a cheap classifier call) and route to a fixed model per category. E.g. intent classification -> Haiku, complex multi-step reasoning -> Sonnet/Opus. No feedback loop, but simple to reason about and audit.

concepts.heading: Cascades: try cheap, escalate on failure
concepts.body: Run the cheap model first. If its output fails a validation check (schema mismatch, low self-reported confidence, a downstream verifier rejecting it), re-run the same request on a more capable model. Pays the cheap-model cost on every request but the expensive-model cost only on the fraction that need it.

concepts.heading: Per-step routing within a single agent loop
concepts.body: A multi-step agent doesn't need the same model for every step. Planning/decomposition may warrant a stronger model; routine tool-call formatting or extraction from already-retrieved text often does not. This requires the agent's orchestration code to make a model choice at each step rather than fixing one model for the whole run.

concepts.heading: Agents-as-Tools: routing as delegation, not just classification
concepts.body: Strands' Agents-as-Tools pattern wraps a specialized Agent in a @tool function so an orchestrator agent can call it like any other tool. This is model routing in a more general form: instead of a single classify-then-pick-model step, the orchestrator (on a capable model) decides per request which specialist agent (each with its own, possibly cheaper, model) to consult -- and can consult more than one, or none, depending on the request.

exercises.title: Build a two-tier cascade with an explicit escalation condition
exercises.goal: Route a classification task to a cheap model by default, and escalate to a stronger model only when the cheap model's output fails validation.
steps: Define a strict output schema for the task (e.g. a JSON object with a required enum field) and a Strands agent per model tier.
Call the cheap-tier agent first. Attempt to parse/validate its output against the schema.
If validation fails, re-run the identical prompt on the strong-tier agent. → Expect: the vast majority of well-formed inputs resolve on the cheap model; only malformed or ambiguous cases escalate.
Log which tier handled each request using each agent's own accumulated_usage. → Expect: over a batch of real inputs, an escalation rate well under 50%, ideally under 15-20% for a well-specified task.

code.content:
import json
from strands import Agent
from strands.models import BedrockModel

SCHEMA_PROMPT = (
    'Respond with only JSON: {"category": "billing"|"technical"|"other", "confidence": "high"|"low"}'
)

cheap_agent = Agent(
    model=BedrockModel(model_id="us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0"),
    callback_handler=None,
)
strong_agent = Agent(
    model=BedrockModel(model_id="us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5"),
    callback_handler=None,
)

def classify_ticket(text):
    prompt = f"Ticket: {text}\n\n{SCHEMA_PROMPT}"

    cheap_response = cheap_agent(prompt)
    try:
        result = json.loads(str(cheap_response))
        if result.get("confidence") == "high" and result.get("category") in {"billing", "technical", "other"}:
            return result["category"], "haiku"
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError):
        pass

    strong_response = strong_agent(prompt)
    result = json.loads(str(strong_response))
    return result["category"], "sonnet-escalated"

exercises.costImpact: If 80% of requests resolve on the cheap tier and only 20% escalate, and the strong model costs 8x the cheap model per call, blended cost is roughly (0.8 x 1) + (0.2 x 8) = 2.4x the cheap-only cost -- versus 8x if every request had gone straight to the strong model. The escalation rate is the number to watch and tune.

exercises.title: Route to a specialist agent with Agents-as-Tools instead of a fixed cascade
exercises.goal: Let an orchestrator agent decide, per request, which cheaper specialist agent to delegate to -- rather than a single always-classify-then-escalate rule.
steps: Build two specialist agents on the cheap model tier, each with a narrow system prompt and only the tools it needs.
Wrap each specialist in a @tool function that calls it and returns its response as a string.
Give an orchestrator agent (on the stronger model tier) only the two specialist tools -- not the underlying work directly.
Send a request that only needs one specialist. → Expect: the orchestrator calls only the relevant specialist tool; the other specialist's model is never invoked, so its cost is zero for that request.
exercises.costImpact: The strong-tier orchestrator only pays for the tool-call decision, not for doing the underlying work -- the actual answer is generated by a cheap-tier specialist. Unused specialists cost nothing per request, unlike a fixed pipeline that always runs every stage.
